title: Wise Business Account Review: Features, Fees, Limitations & More
summary: A review of Wise Business account highlighting features, fees, etc. Read all about how users in Pakistan and Bangladesh can use it and what other options they have.
body_text: If you work with international clients or manage cross-border transactions, you already know how tricky global payments can be. Between currency conversion, transfer delays, and hidden fees, handling money across borders often takes more time than it should. Wise, formerly known as TransferWise, has built a strong reputation as a simple and transparent way to send and receive money globally. But how well does it serve business users in South Asia, especially in Pakistan and Bangladesh, where freelancers, agencies, and exporters make up a fast-growing digital economy? This review looks at what the Wise Business Account offers, how it performs for users in these two countries, and how it compares to alternatives like Elevate Pay, a newer platform built specifically for businesses in emerging markets. What Is a Wise Business Account A Wise Business Account helps you manage global payments from one place. It’s designed for freelancers, exporters, and companies that deal with clients or suppliers overseas. With Wise, you can: Receive and hold funds in more than 40 currencies Send payments to suppliers, contractors, or freelancers around the world Automate recurring and batch payments Integrate your account with accounting tools such as Xero or QuickBooks Everything is managed online through a single dashboard, which makes it simple to track transactions and manage expenses without relying on traditional banks. Wise Business Account in BD & PK Wise Business accounts are available in both Pakistan and Bangladesh, but with some important differences and limitations. While you can open and verify an account online, feature availability and compliance conditions vary from country to country. Availability and Setup You can register your business, verify documents, and set up your account online. Once approved, you can receive international payments from clients or platforms such as Shopify, Amazon, Upwork, or TikTok Shop. However, the onboarding process and feature access can be limited based on local regulations. Many users in Pakistan, for example, have to register under foreign entities or rely on international partners to make full use of Wise’s services. Key Features Send and receive payments in multiple currencies, including USD, EUR, and GBP Access batch and recurring payments for payroll or supplier management Connect to business tools for easier bookkeeping and expense tracking Limitations and Restrictions While Wise is reliable for global payments, there are certain limitations that matter if your business is based in the South Asian region: Limited or unavailable debit cards in both Pakistan and Bangladesh Restricted inbound transfers in some cases Focused primarily on international transactions, not local banking In short, Wise works well for moving money across borders, but not as a full banking solution for businesses that also need local integration or compliance features. Who Wise Business Works Best For Wise is a good fit if you primarily work with international clients or partners. It works best for: Freelancers and agencies receiving global payments E-commerce sellers exporting products through Amazon or Shopify Businesses paying international vendors or remote teams If you operate globally and only need to send or receive payments, Wise is a solid choice. But if your business also needs payroll, compliance, or local settlement options, you may find the experience limited. Wise Business Account in Pakistan In Pakistan, Wise is often used by freelancers and digital entrepreneurs who receive funds from clients abroad. The setup is simple, but some restrictions apply: You can receive international payments in major currencies Funds can be sent to a local Pakistani bank account, converted to PKR There are no PKR receiving accounts, and debit card availability is limited Some users report difficulty linking Wise to local banks for full functionality Despite these hurdles, Wise remains a popular option for exporters and freelancers managing foreign income. Wise Business Account in Bangladesh In Bangladesh, Wise allows users to hold and send payments in multiple currencies. It’s widely used by freelancers, outsourcing firms, and small e-commerce sellers. However, like in Pakistan, certain features are limited. You can link your Wise account to receive payments from marketplaces and clients abroad, but local banking features such as debit cards and BDT receiving accounts are not available. Wise focuses on cross-border payments rather than domestic transactions. Pricing and Fees Wise is known for transparent pricing. You always see the true exchange rate before completing a transfer, which makes it easy to understand how much you’re paying. Typical fees include: A small percentage per transaction, usually between 0.4% and 1.2% Conversion fees when switching currencies A one-time setup fee in some regions for business accounts For most users, these fees are lower than what traditional banks charge. However, if your business processes a large number of international payments or frequent currency conversions, the costs can add up over time. Pros and Cons Summary Pros Transparent pricing with no hidden fees Access to 40+ currencies Batch payments and accounting integrations Works well for international freelancers and exporters Cons Debit cards may not be available in some regions Local regulatory restrictions can limit features Primarily built for international transactions, not domestic finance Alternatives to Wise for South Asian Businesses While Wise is strong for global payments, many South Asian businesses need more flexibility. They want a solution that combines international payment access with local financial management, especially when it comes to payroll and compliance. Some global alternatives include Payoneer and Revolut, but both have limitations in local integration and regional support. For a platform built specifically for freelancers, startups, and e-commerce businesses in this region, Elevate Pay stands out as a more complete option. Elevate Pay: The Better Choice for BD and PK Businesses If you are based in Bangladesh or Pakistan and your business earns globally, Elevate Pay is designed for you. It connects international payment rails with the local financial ecosystem, helping you do more than just receive funds. You can open business accounts that work with major networks such as ACH, domestic wire, and SWIFT. This means you can receive USD directly from clients, platforms, or global marketplaces like Amazon FBA, Upwork, and Fiverr. Built for Modern Global Businesses Elevate Pay supports both US-incorporated businesses owned by Bangladeshi founders and locally registered companies receiving export income. It’s ideal for agencies, SaaS startups, dev shops, remote teams, and freelancers who need access to USD accounts and compliant local operations. Simplified Payroll and Payouts Through its Payroll Power-up, you can send payments to team members locally in BDT or globally in USD. You can run batch payouts, save on fees and conversion costs, and keep every transaction traceable, all within one unified dashboard. A Web-First Experience Everything happens online. You can manage transfers, monitor balances, and handle both incoming and outgoing payments through a clean, simple interface. There’s no need to juggle multiple platforms or tools. Why Elevate Pay Fits Better Platforms like Wise focus on global infrastructure. Elevate Pay focuses on regional usability, helping South Asian businesses connect their international income with local growth. It brings together payments, payroll, and compliance in a way that feels natural for freelancers and digital companies in this region. Conclusion Wise remains one of the most trusted names in international payments. It’s transparent, efficient, and perfect for straightforward cross-border transfers. But for businesses in Pakistan and Bangladesh, the gaps are clear. Wise is built for a global audience, not necessarily for the unique challenges of South Asian entrepreneurs. If your goal is to simply send and receive payments abroad, Wise gets the job done. But if you want to build a business around your global income, manage teams, and stay locally compliant, Elevate Pay is a better fit. It brings the entire financial workflow together, from receiving USD to paying your team and tracking compliance, all in one place.

title: Bloom Apps Now Support App Clips
summary: Anyone can now try a Bloom app from a link on iOS without downloading or installing anything.
body_text: Changelog November 19, 2025 Bloom Apps Now Support App Clips Anyone can now try a Bloom app from a link on iOS without downloading or installing anything. When you share your app link, iPhone users who don't have it installed will get an App Clip experience instead of a blank page. They can use the core features of your app immediately, right from the share sheet or a browser tap. This is useful for a few things: Sharing with people who won't install an app If you're showing your app to someone and don't want to ask them to go to the App Store, send them the link. It just works. Getting faster feedback Testers can try your app without any friction. No TestFlight, no setup. App Clip support is on by default for all Bloom apps. Nothing to configure.

title: Best CMMS for Gyms 2026: Top 8 Fitness Facility Management Solutions Matt Velker Matt Velker November 10, 2025
summary: Compare the top 8 CMMS solutions for gyms and fitness centers. Find the right software to manage equipment maintenance, reduce downtime, and retain members.
body_text: In This Post A Note On The Importance of Gym-Specific Integrations Processing Warranty Repairs and OEM Coordination How We Compare the Best CMMS for Gyms 8 Best CMMS for Gyms: Platform Reviews Choose the Right CMMS for Your Gym In This Post A Note On The Importance of Gym-Specific Integrations Processing Warranty Repairs and OEM Coordination How We Compare the Best Facilities Management Software for Gyms What matters (and why) 8 Best Facilities Management Software for Gyms: Platform Reviews OpenWrench ServiceChannel Corrigo Vixxo Ecotrack Fexa UpKeep FitnessEMS Choose the Right Facilities Management Software for Your Gym Running a gym is expensive. Between equipment, utilities, and staffing, every decision affects profitability. Industry data shows that the average gym spends around $20,000 per month (on the lower end) to stay operational, and equipment maintenance alone can reach 3–5% of each machine’s original cost annually. This means maintaining a $2,500 treadmill costs roughly $750–$125 each year — and that’s just one asset. When critical systems like HVAC fail, losses extend beyond repairs to downtime, member dissatisfaction, and revenue disruption. This is why proactive maintenance is no longer optional. The right computerized maintenance management system (CMMS) helps gym operators automate upkeep, track costs, and reduce unplanned downtime that disrupts operations and impacts retention. This guide compares the best CMMS software solutions for gyms and fitness facilities, detailing which systems best meet gym-specific needs. A Note On The Importance of Gym-Specific Integrations Integrations make a CMMS truly gym-ready. Most gyms use several disconnected systems for membership, billing, and equipment management. When these tools don’t communicate, visibility drops and manual work increases. Connecting a CMMS to gym management platforms like Mindbody , ABC Fitness , and Club OS solves this problem. It syncs maintenance with real usage data, automates reporting, and reduces administrative effort. Unified APIs — such as those offered by OpenWrench — extend this efficiency to maintenance, linking equipment data and member systems to improve reliability and streamline operations. Processing Warranty Repairs and OEM Coordination Warranty repairs are one of the last maintenance workflows most gyms still manage manually. While platforms like OpenWrench automate work orders, inspections, and vendor coordination, warranty claims with equipment manufacturers typically remain disconnected — tracked through original equipment manufacturer ( OEM) portals rather than integrated software. Most major fitness brands use online warranty portals that let operators register equipment, submit service requests, and track repair progress. Claims must be authorized by the manufacturer and routed to approved service providers before parts are repaired or replaced. The process works, but it’s slow — turnaround times often stretch two to eight weeks depending on parts and approvals. During that time, key machines sit idle, frustrating members and cutting into revenue. Today, these OEM systems rarely connect directly with facility management tools. Matrix and Core , for example, maintain integrations with fitness-tracking ecosystems like EGYM and Myzone , not maintenance software. This gap leaves operators manually logging warranty work orders and following up on claim statuses across multiple systems. This is where OpenWrench adds value. The platform centralizes warranty information, service history, and part replacements in one place. Even when OEMs require external claim submission, facilities teams still have a clear record of what’s covered, what’s pending, and what’s next. By combining warranty tracking with preventive maintenance workflows , OpenWrench helps gyms reduce downtime, avoid duplicate repairs, and recover more value under warranty coverage. Across the manufacturing world, automated warranty systems have been shown to cut processing costs and claim cycle times while improving customer satisfaction. For gyms, adopting CMMS platforms like OpenWrench extends these same benefits to equipment management — transforming warranty repair from a slow, manual task into a transparent, data-driven process. How We Compare the Best CMMS for Gyms Choosing the right cloud-based CMMS software requires more than comparing feature lists. The goal is to find a platform that fits your operational complexity, budget, and growth plans. Below is how we evaluated each option and why these criteria matter for day-to-day gym operations. What matters (and why) To evaluate each platform fairly, we focused on the core capabilities that drive results in a fitness environment. These areas directly impact uptime, costs, and member experience. Pricing: Transparent pricing helps you forecast return on investment (ROI) and avoid hidden per‑user or implementation charges. For multi‑site gyms, unclear fees can turn a good tool into an unexpected budget risk. Integrations: The CMMS should connect with enterprise resource planning (ERP)/accounting and vendor networks, along with other core management tools. Clean data flows make approvals, purchase orders, and cost allocation faster and more accurate. Customer support: When a critical asset is down, response time matters. Look for onboarding help, training resources, and fast access to technical support. Ease of use: If the mobile app is hard to use, adoption drops. We looked for clear workflows, user-friendly interfaces, and mobile-first experiences. Key features: Work order management, preventive maintenance (PM) scheduling, asset management, vendor management, and real-time dashboards form the baseline. Strong analytics and performance metrics turn maintenance data into decisions. Together, these factors separate systems your teams tolerate from systems they champion . With this framework set, here’s how the top CMMS platforms for gyms compare — and what makes each stand out. 8 Best CMMS for Gyms: Platform Reviews Now that we’ve outlined the key evaluation criteria, let’s look at how the top contenders stack up. Each CMMS platform below serves a distinct type of gym or facility operation — from small studios to nationwide franchises. This section breaks down the strengths, weaknesses, and standout features of each option so you can identify which system best fits your needs. 1. OpenWrench Best for: Multi‑location gyms and franchises that need real‑time visibility, vendor control, and fast rollout. OpenWrench is an all‑in‑one facility management platform designed to streamline maintenance operations across many sites without adding complexity. It centralizes maintenance work orders, PM, vendor coordination, and spend tracking in one mobile‑first system. Key features OpenWrench focuses on speed to value for busy maintenance teams while covering the essentials. Automated work orders : Create, assign, and track maintenance tasks with real‑time status and notifications. Preventive maintenance scheduling: Automate recurring tasks to reduce downtime and keep assets compliant. Comprehensive asset management: Track equipment warranties, service history, and lifecycle costs from a single dashboard to maintain visibility across all locations. Vendor scorecards: Compare response times, first‑time‑fix rates, and cost trends across locations. Mobile app : Empower onsite staff to submit photos, notes, and work orders instantly — without training headaches. Together, these features give facility leaders visibility into workloads and spending while keeping local teams focused on member experience. For growing fitness brands, it’s the balance of functionality and simplicity that sets OpenWrench apart. Pros OpenWrench offers several clear advantages for gym operators who want to save time and increase visibility across multiple locations. Fast implementation — most operators go live in weeks, not months Hands‑on onboarding and responsive customer support Customizable checklists, dashboards, and approval flows by location Real‑time insights into vendor performance and maintenance costs The overall result is a platform that keeps gyms running efficiently and helps operators control costs without technical friction. Cons While OpenWrench performs well for most operators, there are a few limitations to consider before rollout. Fewer pre‑built third‑party integrations than some enterprise platforms Even with these trade‑offs, OpenWrench’s ease of use and fast setup make it a top contender for multi‑location operators. 2. ServiceChannel Best for: Large fitness chains managing complex vendor networks and compliance across 500+ locations who don't mind paying a bit more. ServiceChannel operates at enterprise scale, processing millions of work orders annually through a large network of providers. It emphasizes standardization, compliance, and granular analytics for operators who need strict control across markets. Key features ServiceChannel goes deep on vendor and compliance management. SLA‑tracked work orders: Automate dispatch and manage proposals with service‑level agreement tracking. Preventive maintenance: Set recurring schedules and store documentation for audits and inspections. Real‑time spend analytics: View dashboards and key performance indicators (KPIs) for leadership visibility and cost control. Large provider network: Access a wide network of vetted contractors for faster sourcing. This breadth suits organizations that prioritize centralized control and governance. Operators who need robust analytics and a vast vendor network will find ServiceChannel’s depth hard to match. Pros ServiceChannel’s strengths are most apparent for enterprise operations managing dozens or hundreds of facilities. Proven scalability for hundreds or thousands of locations Detailed analytics for spend, vendor efficiency, and lifecycle costs Enterprise‑grade security and compliance tooling For large-scale franchises, this combination ensures predictability and strong vendor accountability. Cons There are also some drawbacks to weigh before investing in ServiceChannel. Longer implementations (often measured in months) Steeper learning curve; training is typically required Pricing is not published and tends to fit larger budgets Vendor fees charged by platform can increase service provider pricing Smaller organizations may find that the cost and setup time outweigh the benefits of such a comprehensive solution. 3. Corrigo Best for: Large organizations moving from reactive firefighting to proactive maintenance. Backed by JLL Technologies, Corrigo brings enterprise infrastructure and automation to facilities management. It’s built to handle high work-order volumes without performance degradation. Key features Corrigo’s strength is workflow automation at scale. Skill-based routing: Match jobs with qualified technicians automatically. PM automation: Generate and track tasks with asset data integrated. Analytics dashboards: Monitor vendor compliance, costs, and performance in real time. AI-assisted dispatch: Optimize technician assignment based on availability and proximity. These automation tools make Corrigo a powerhouse for large, complex portfolios. Its analytics and routing features save time for facilities teams juggling hundreds of tickets. Pros Corrigo offers enterprise reliability for teams that need automation at scale. Reliable performance at very high volumes Deep automation reduces manual coordination Access to large provider networks across markets Operators who manage dispersed regional or national gym brands will appreciate Corrigo’s ability to keep up with demand. Cons Despite its strengths, Corrigo’s complexity may pose challenges for smaller operators. Configuration requires time and dedicated expertise More complexity than most single-brand gym operators need Ultimately, Corrigo is a strong choice for companies with the internal resources to manage its sophistication. 4. Vixxo Best for: Enterprises that want a managed services model alongside software. Vixxo combines a CMMS platform with outsourced vendor coordination. For teams that prefer to offload contractor sourcing and day-to-day dispatch, the hybrid model can reduce internal overhead. Key features Vixxo provides maintenance management software plus services under one roof. Work order tracking: Maintain centralized oversight with automated reporting. Managed vendor coordination: Let Vixxo’s team handle contractor sourcing and scheduling. Multi-site reporting: Review spending and performance across all properties from one dashboard. This approach suits operators who value single-partner simplicity over hands-on control. It’s particularly useful for brands expanding into new regions where local vendor relationships aren’t yet established. Pros Vixxo provides operational relief for organizations that prefer to outsource vendor management. Lower internal burden for vendor management Consistent maintenance processes across markets For enterprise operators, the ability to outsource vendor management can translate to faster response times and fewer internal bottlenecks. Cons There are also trade-offs for teams that value transparency and control. Limited visibility into vendor selection and performance details Support responsiveness may vary depending on account size Smaller gym chains may prefer a CMMS that keeps vendor control in-house for greater flexibility. 5. Ecotrak Best for: Operators focused on cost visibility, forecasting, and data-driven decisions. Ecotrak balances core CMMS functionality with strong financial analytics. It’s built for teams that want to understand today’s spend and predict tomorrow’s. Key features Ecotrak makes maintenance financials easier to manage. Automated work orders: Manage requests through completion and invoicing. Asset tracking: Monitor equipment performance and lifecycle data to plan replacements and control costs. Predictive maintenance analytics: Forecast spend, anticipate equipment failures, and identify potential savings opportunities. ERP/accounting integrations: Connect systems for accurate cost allocation. These tools help facilities leaders defend budgets and identify savings. For operators who live in spreadsheets, Ecotrak’s insights turn maintenance data into actionable business intelligence. Pros Ecotrak appeals to financially driven operators who want detailed cost forecasting. Real-time cost visibility with forecasting Data-driven insights for repair-vs-replace decisions The platform appeals to teams ready to connect facilities management with finance. Cons Ecotrak’s sophistication comes with a few drawbacks for smaller gyms. Data-dense interface can feel heavy to new users Pricing often exceeds simpler CMMS tools For cost-conscious gym operators, Ecotrak may deliver more analytics than they need for the price. 6. Fexa Best for: Growing gym brands that want enterprise-grade automation without enterprise bloat. Fexa sits between lightweight apps and heavyweight platforms. It supports 10 to 100+ locations with strong automation and cost control. Key features Fexa focuses on vendor transparency and PM coverage. Automated dispatch: Route service calls based on skill, geography, and performance. Vendor scorecards: Track response time, pricing trends, and service quality. PM scheduling and invoice compliance: Prevent overbilling and missed maintenance. Role-based dashboards: Let each user see the data most relevant to their role. These features give teams insight into performance and budgets while keeping daily operations simple. For mid-sized operators, Fexa delivers a practical mix of structure and flexibility. Pros Fexa delivers measurable operational gains for scaling organizations. Measurable savings via vendor accountability Better coordination between operations and finance The result is a platform that helps operators catch inefficiencies before they affect uptime. Cons Fexa isn’t without limitations. More setup than very simple tools Some integrations require custom work Still, for brands scaling beyond ten locations, Fexa provides long-term value and stability. 7. UpKeep Best for: Gyms that need a user-friendly CMMS for maintenance scheduling, work order management, and team communication. UpKeep is one of the most popular cloud-based CMMS platforms among fitness facilities and recreation centers. It’s built for ease of use, helping maintenance teams manage assets, track repairs, and communicate in real time through a simple mobile app. Key features UpKeep focuses on accessibility and day-to-day maintenance visibility. Work order management: Create and assign tasks instantly from desktop or mobile devices. Preventive maintenance scheduling: Automate recurring tasks to reduce downtime and extend equipment lifespan. Asset tracking and reporting: Record maintenance history, costs, and performance metrics for every machine. Inventory management: Track spare parts and supplies to prevent delays and stockouts. These features make UpKeep ideal for gyms seeking a straightforward maintenance management solution that improves communication between staff and vendors while keeping operations organized. Pros UpKeep stands out for its simplicity and fast adoption. User-friendly interface and quick setup with minimal training Strong mobile app for technicians and on-site staff It’s particularly effective for gyms that want to modernize maintenance tracking without a long learning curve. Cons UpKeep’s focus on usability means a few advanced capabilities are limited. Reporting and analytics are lighter than enterprise-grade systems Integration options are fewer compared to larger CMMS platforms For most operators, however, UpKeep offers the right balance of functionality, flexibility, and simplicity. 8. FitnessEMS Best for: Health clubs that want an industry-specific CMMS tailored to gym equipment. FitnessEMS is purpose-built for fitness facilities. Workflows map cleanly to how gyms operate, from front-desk reporting to maintenance resolution. Key features FitnessEMS makes equipment-level reporting fast and familiar. QR code scans: Allow staff or members to report issues instantly. Gym-specific PM templates: Use prebuilt maintenance schedules for treadmills and other gym equipment. Vendor linking: Keep communication logs and completion tracking in one place. Member impact views: Connect maintenance performance directly to member satisfaction. By focusing only on fitness equipment, FitnessEMS shortens implementation time and improves accuracy in reporting. It’s designed for teams who want quick wins and minimal setup. Pros FitnessEMS delivers efficiency for equipment-heavy environments. Minimal training due to fitness-first design Noticeable downtime reduction via quick reporting For gyms focused purely on equipment uptime, it provides an intuitive, niche solution. Cons There are trade-offs in focusing solely on gym equipment. Limited integrations outside fitness-focused stacks Gaps for non-fitness assets (pools, spas, childcare) in mixed-use facilities Operators with more diverse facilities may find its specialization restrictive. Choose the Right CMMS for Your Gym Choosing the right CMMS depends on your gym’s size and complexity. Smaller studios often prefer simple, mobile‑first systems for quick setup. Larger organizations look for platforms that offer scalability and centralized oversight. Most operators fall between these extremes — they need automation and visibility without enterprise‑level complexity. Cost and value should be evaluated together. Some systems include extra fees for integrations or training, but the best solutions still deliver measurable savings through better uptime and more efficient maintenance. A reliable CMMS for gyms also improves safety tracking to help gyms stay compliant and minimize risk. title: Palatin Reports First Quarter Fiscal Year 2026 Financial Results and Provides Corporate Update
summary: Nov 13, 2025, 07:30 ET Significant progress on multiple fronts – obesity pipeline advancing towards the clinic, out-licensing collaboration, strengthened balance sheet, and reinstatement of NYSE American trading Melanocortin-based therapies for obesity PL7737 IND-enabling toxicology underway; IND submission and clinical trial initiation planned for the first half of 2026 Next-generation selective peptide MC4R agonists d esigned […]
body_text: Nov 13, 2025, 07:30 ET Significant progress on multiple fronts – obesity pipeline advancing towards the clinic, out-licensing collaboration, strengthened balance sheet, and reinstatement of NYSE American trading Melanocortin-based therapies for obesity PL7737 IND-enabling toxicology underway; IND submission and clinical trial initiation planned for the first half of 2026 Next-generation selective peptide MC4R agonists d esigned for once-weekly subcutaneous dosing; IND submission and clinical trial initiation planned for mid-2026 Research Collaboration, License and Patent Assignment Agreement with Boehringer Ingelheim for the treatment of retinal diseases in August 2025 Received €2.0M ($2.3M) upfront Achieved €5.5M ($6.5M) research milestone in September 2025 $18.2 million public offering, including full exercise of the over-allotment option, closed on November 12, 2025 Regained compliance with NYSE American listing standards – common stock resumed trading under the symbol “PTN” on November 12, 2025 Teleconference and Webcast to be held on Thursday, November 13, 2025, at 11:00 AM EST PRINCETON, N.J. , Nov. 13, 2025 /PRNewswire/ — Palatin Technologies, Inc. (NYSE American: PTN), a biopharmaceutical company developing first-in-class medicines based on molecules that modulate the activity of the melanocortin receptor (MCR) system, today announced financial results for its fiscal first quarter ended September 30, 2025 and provided a corporate update. “Palatin’s melanocortin-based obesity programs are advancing rapidly, led by our oral small molecule PL7737, which is on track to enter clinical studies in the first half of next year,” said Carl Spana, Ph.D., President and CEO of Palatin “The strength of our preclinical data and our ability to target both broad and rare obesity indications – particularly neuroendocrine diseases such as hypothalamic obesity, underscore the differentiated potential of our melanocortin platform and our commitment to transforming obesity treatment.” “The execution of our collaboration with Boehringer Ingelheim, completion of our $18.2 million public offering, and reinstatement of NYSE American trading mark an important inflection point for Palatin,” continued Dr. Spana. “As we move into 2026, we are well positioned with a strengthened balance sheet, a global partnership delivering near-term milestones, and a robust pipeline of clinical catalysts that collectively support meaningful long-term value creation.” Obesity Program Update PL7737 (oral MC4R agonist): Demonstrated robust weight loss, strong safety, and high oral bioavailability in preclinical models. IND-enabling toxicology studies are ongoing, with an IND filing and initiation of a Phase 1 single- and multiple-ascending dose (SAD/MAD) trial expected in the first half of 2026. Phase 1 studies are planned to include patients with hypothalamic obesity. The U.S. FDA has granted Orphan Drug Designation for the treatment of leptin receptor (LEPR) deficiency–related obesity. Next-generation selective peptide MC4R agonists: Designed for once-weekly subcutaneous dosing, with an IND filing and Phase 1 SAD/MAD trial planned for mid-2026. Phase 1 studies are also expected to include patients with hypothalamic obesity. Pre-clinical and early clinical data support co-administration with tirzepatide as a safe, potentially synergistic approach to weight management. Out-Licensing Programs Update Retinal diseases (MCR agonists) – Boehringer Ingelheim collaboration Received an upfront payment of €2.0 million ($2.3 million) in August 2025. Achieved €5.5 million ($6.5 million) research milestone in September 2025. Eligible to receive up to €12.5 million ($14.5 million) in additional near-term research milestones and up to €260 million ($307.0 million) in development, regulatory, and commercial milestones, plus tiered royalties on future net sales. PL9643 (MCR agonist) – Dry Eye Disease Reported positive Phase 3 MELODY-1 results, with 6 of 13 symptom endpoints showing statistically significant complete symptom resolution versus placebo (p<0.05). Out-licensing discussions are ongoing. PL8177 (MCR agonist) – Ulcerative Colitis Achieved positive Phase 2 proof-of-concept results. Out-licensing discussions are ongoing. Melanocortin-4 Receptor Agonists Effect on Obesity Hypothalamic neurons expressing the melanocortin-4 receptor (MC4R) play a central role in regulating stored energy, food intake, and body weight. Genetic mutations that inhibit signaling through the MC4R pathway lead to hyperphagia, decreased energy expenditure and early-onset obesity; such mutations have been identified as the cause of several rare genetic obesity disorders. MC4R agonism represents an attractive target for potential obesity treatments. About Hypothalamic Obesity Hypothalamic obesity is a rare and severe form of obesity caused by dysfunction or damage to the hypothalamus, the region of the brain that regulates appetite, satiety, and energy balance. Hypothalamic obesity can occur as an acquired condition, most commonly after surgery or radiation therapy for brain tumors such as craniopharyngioma, or as a congenital disorder associated with genetic syndromes and developmental abnormalities affecting hypothalamic function. Individuals with hypothalamic obesity typically experience rapid, excessive weight gain, uncontrollable hunger, and profound metabolic disturbances that are resistant to conventional diet, exercise, and behavioral interventions. There are currently no approved pharmacologic treatments specifically indicated for hypothalamic obesity, representing a significant unmet medical need. About Melanocortin Receptor Agonists The melanocortin receptor (“MCR”) system has effects on inflammation, immune system responses, metabolism, food intake, and sexual function. There are five melanocortin receptors, MC1R through MC5R. Modulation of these receptors, through use of receptor-specific agonists, which activate receptor function, or receptor-specific antagonists, which block receptor function, can have medically significant pharmacological effects. About Palatin Palatin is a biopharmaceutical company developing first-in-class medicines based on molecules that modulate the activity of the melanocortin receptor systems, with targeted, receptor-specific product candidates for the treatment of diseases with significant unmet medical need and commercial potential. Palatin’s strategy is to develop products and then form marketing collaborations with industry leaders to maximize their commercial potential. title: TMS for construction: How transportation management systems simplify fleet operations
summary: Looking to streamline delivery logistics and scale? Here's how a transportation management system helps you do just that.
body_text: If you’re a booker at a construction material distribution company, you’ve got a big job on your hands. From dedicated routes to LTL shipments to last-minute hotshots , everything needs to go out as expected to keep operations afloat. That job is made easier with a TMS. Here’s what it is, and five benefits TMS software has on construction distributor route planning . What is a TMS? A transportation management system, or TMS , is a software application that helps businesses manage the logistics that come with scheduling and executing deliveries. The TMS is part of the larger supply chain system, focusing on optimizing delivery routes, tracking freight status en route, and automating the tedious to-dos that are part of the process. The point of the TMS is to reduce time spent and save money for both the distributor and the end customer. App and cloud-based technologies have greatly improved TMS effectiveness, as the construction industry has long relied on manual processes rather than embracing technology. The accessibility of recent TMS tools also allows businesses of all sizes to streamline their processes without breaking the bank. How TMS systems improve construction material distributor operations: 5 benefits 1. Real-time delivery tracking The construction business is unpredictable. There’s always a need for deep coordination, but the industry's nature also demands agility and flexibility. By supporting live tracking, a TMS can offer a window into the precise location and status of deliveries, something any business will soon discover is indispensable. Real-time tracking also means reduced idle time at the point of distribution and delivery. Project completion times are met, trust is built between distributor and customer, and everybody wins. 2. Optimized scheduling and planning When businesses opt for a TMS, every delivery is planned to be as efficient as possible. These systems use AI and other tech to monitor live traffic, account for route length and delivery windows, and more to ensure every booking is as optimal as possible. The TMS also continuously learns, so companies can continue to schedule in the best possible way. They help businesses identify and address inefficiencies, thereby reducing unnecessary travel for their internal team, minimizing fuel costs, and improving timelines. 3. Better internal resource allocation If we had to bet, we’d say your internal fleet is already stretched thin. This means that maintaining efficiency and meeting customers’ last-minute requests are nearly impossible. And scaling? Forget about it. But a proper TMS will allow distributors to ensure each route and task is assigned in a way that shrinks idle time and maximizes productivity. If your TMS system also doubles as a 3PL system like Curri , you’ll know exactly where you need to fill the gaps your internal fleet can’t. This smart route planning capability is crucial, especially when you have a limited team, someone has a sick day, or a new client needs emergency materials by end of day. 4. Better collaboration and visibility for all stakeholders Effective communication in the construction business bridges gaps among teams, distributors, and stakeholders. And route visibility is a big part of that. A good TMS will provide live tracking visibility not just to the booker, but to everyone who needs insight into the ETA of materials. On top of that, proof of delivery is key. If a driver can collect a signature and a photo of a completed delivery, everyone gets the peace of mind of knowing the material got to where it needed to go. It also confirms the optimal receiving location for future deliveries. 5. Reduced operational costs Every tool and app floods businesses with data these days, but few know what to do with it. A great TMS will use live data and historical trip data to automatically match you with the right driver, vehicle, and route to get your trip done right today. No need to sift through or think about how to use the data to your advantage. The app does it for you with smarter, automated strategic planning. Why Curri makes a great TMS (and more!) You may know of Curri as a way to book drivers and deliveries quickly, but you might not know it’s a complete, comprehensive logistics platform . Curri’s highly intuitive route planner helps businesses of all sizes streamline their delivery logistics in three ways, including: Drag-and-drop: Curri users can easily drag orders from a queue right into a driver’s route for quick bookings and adjustments. Lasso tool: Users can also simply draw a delivery “loop” zone around all applicable drop-off points and assign that route to a driver. AI auto-assign: Users can also try Curri’s advanced AI-powered auto-assign feature. This method uses advanced logic to automatically build complex driver routes. Users can even run scenarios to minimize vehicle use. It saves any booker’s time while the business saves money. And to add another layer of organization, Curri’s calendar view lets bookers and dispatchers see all outgoing routes at a glance. This helps everyone stay on track, on time, and able to scale. Here’s how Curri’s route planner compares to a simple or manual TMS system. Requires manual typing, copying, or drawing routes. Changes are slow and error-prone. Route Creation The lasso tool optimizes delivery zones by drawing a loop around drop-offs. It’s fast and visual. Booker must manually map addresses and group stops, often guessing the best clustering. Optimization Logic AI auto-assign builds complex, efficient routes automatically, minimizing vehicles and time spent. No optimization engine; relies on human judgment, which can lead to inefficiencies and missed savings. Scenario Planning Users can run “what-if” scenarios to test route options before booking. Hard to model scenarios manually; requires extra spreadsheets, maps, and time. Visibility Calendar view displays all upcoming routes at a glance for whole-team alignment. Limited visibility; typically scattered across notes, emails, texts, or whiteboards. Accuracy & Consistency System-driven logic ensures consistent routing decisions across planners. Outcomes vary depending on who is planning, their skill level, and time available. Scalability Designed to support rapid growth with automated tools. Difficult to scale. Planning becomes unmanageable beyond a small fleet. title: How to Approach Healthy Eating During the Holidays
summary: Pediatrician and mom of three Joana Fraser, MD shares ways parents can help their kids enjoy the holiday treats without overindulging.
body_text: This blog is for informational purposes only and does not provide medical advice; see our full disclaimer for more information. ‘Tis the season for colorful candies, cute cookies, and plates full of carb-heavy deliciousness. While it’s true the holidays are a time for culinary indulgence for the fam, it’s the responsibility of parents to ensure our kids aren’t going too far and help them to make healthy choices as much as possible. How to Avoid Overindulgence on Sweet Treats While kids don’t believe there’s such a thing as too many treats, parents know otherwise. As Board-certified pediatrician and mom of three, Joanna Fraser, MD says, “setting boundaries around treats and, most importantly, sticking to these boundaries can help to avoid too much overindulgence or too many tantrums.” Just as you would during other times, it’s important during the holidays to set rules when it comes to sweet treats. “For example, your house rule could be one treat per day, always at a certain time (e.g. after or with dinner).” Knowing that the yummy treat is coming can sometimes help your little one with being patient. You can, of course, make exceptions—like extra treats on Thanksgiving Day or Christmas Eve—that make sense for your kiddo. Just be sure to be clear about the boundaries and the exceptions, as kids look to their parents for guidance and consistency. How to Minimize Snacking Time off from school means schedules are in flux and your kiddo may want to fill the time with unnecessary snacking. Here again, Dr. Fraser highlights the importance of boundaries. “Make snacks available only at certain times of the day and give a short list of snack choices. If it’s not on the menu, it’s not available!” If you find your child is screaming that they’re “starving” even though they just ate a meal (we’ve all heard this one), you can offer a healthy snack—it’s the best way to check if they’re truly hungry. Because if they are STARVING, carrot sticks or apple slices should do the trick! How to Handle Healthy Eating While Traveling When it comes to traveling, there are lots of unknowns as your routine is shaken up and access to your chosen foods may be limited. Packing healthy snacks for the journey is a great way to infuse some consistency into your little one’s diet. For example, Dr. Fraser suggests our Refrigerated Oat Bars , pouches , and other snacks —whatever your nutritious go-tos at home are! This can help minimize those emergency purchases of unhealthy snacks. “Try to focus on one meal a day which is wholesome and eaten together as a family,” she suggests, “but also try not to stress too much about how there will be more treats and less healthy foods eaten over this period.” Check out our other tips for prioritizing healthy eating while traveling ! How to Balance a Heavy, Unbalanced Meal It’s the holidays, which means carbs galore. You can try to balance this by offering lots of healthy choices before big meals. “If you know dinner might be carb-heavy,” Dr. Fraser says, “serve a big platter of colorful fruits and veggies and various dips.” Try sliced carrots or peppers with hummus or peanut butter with fresh fruit. “This will serve to ensure they eat some healthy food and also make their tummies fuller before the main meal so they might eat less of the unhealthy options on the table!” How to Talk with Your Kids About Healthy Eating During the Holidays When it comes to talking about food with your kids, Dr. Fraser suggests avoiding labeling foods as ‘good’ or ‘bad’. “Instead,” she explains, “talk about how certain foods are better for helping our bodies grow, learn, and have lots of energy.” Other foods taste good and they are fun—and OK—to eat in small amounts, but they don’t help our bodies. On the contrary, they can also make us feel tired and yucky. “Emphasize how much fun we have when our bodies feel good, so we want to make sure we are treating our bodies well so we can feel strong and energetic every day!” Try to avoid stressing them out or creating negative associations with food, but rather focus on the great things the right foods can do for us. Eating tasty foods during the holidays is a privilege and an experience we want our kids to be a part of. It’s all about finding the right balance and ensuring you and your littles ones are still prioritizing healthy, balanced meals and not overindulging in the treats and snacks, even though they are SO tasty!
